reason: The text features the people (העם) and individual men (אִישׁ) as regular human characters with demonstrated agency. They perform multiple actions: they go out (יצאוּ), gather manna (לקטוּ), make choices about when to gather, and even refuse to keep God's commandments (מאנתם). Most notably, on the seventh day, the people independently choose to go out and gather—a volitional action that violates God's instruction—demonstrating their capacity for autonomous decision-making, even when it conflicts with divine command. They also 'rest' (שבתוּ) on the seventh day, showing obedience as another exercised choice. These are not mere passive recipients of divine action but agents whose behavior drives the narrative.
